name: DHEA (dehydroepiandrosterone, prasterone)
short: Case reports: mania after starting DHEA, in one case with threats to kill. A trial in women with fibromyalgia found more androgenic effects (acne, greasy skin, body hair); HDL fell in women.
text: Case reports describe mania after starting DHEA: a 31-year-old man, who had once been given an unsubstantiated diagnosis of bipolar disorder and used alcohol episodically, developed mood and behaviour changes several weeks after starting it and was committed involuntarily after threatening to kill himself, family members and a friend, and an older man with no personal or family history of bipolar disorder was admitted with mania that appeared related to DHEA he had started 6 months earlier; the authors of the first report named high doses, a history of mood disorder, concurrent use of alcohol, street drugs or antidepressants, and cytochrome P450 polymorphisms as uncertain potential risk factors, and said that use under age 35 may be especially risky because the body's own DHEA levels peak at age 20 to 30. In a 3-month randomised crossover trial in 52 postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia, androgenic side effects (greasy skin, acne and increased growth of body hair) were more common during DHEA treatment, and a 2022 review of DHEA in women states that the androgenic and estrogenic side effects of high physiologic or pharmacologic use are of concern for long-term use. A meta-analysis of randomised trials (23 articles) found no change in total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol or triglycerides but a reduction in HDL cholesterol, significant in studies of women but not of men; another meta-analysis of randomised trials found no significant change in the liver enzymes AST and ALT but a significant fall in serum cortisol (by about 54 nmol/L, pooled from 10 trial arms), and a Cochrane review of trials in older adults found DHEA well tolerated apart from poorer visual memory recall after a stressor in one trial, and called for trials lasting longer than one year. In postmenopausal women with moderate to severe pain during sex due to vulvovaginal atrophy, prasterone applied inside the vagina daily showed no significant drug-related side effects in pooled data from three 12-week placebo-controlled trials (436 women treated, 260 given placebo). Apart from the possible risk factors named in the case report, no interaction data were found in the cited sources.
